stem.text: The concentration of a medicine in a patient's blood is modeled by \( C(t) = 100 - 55 e^{- \frac{t}{8}} \) milligrams per liter, for \( 0 \le t \le 24 \), where t is measured in hours. Using a calculator, find \( C'(8) \), showing the setup, and interpret the value in the context of the problem with correct units. Give the value correct to three decimal places.

answer_key.label: \( C'(8) = 2.529 \), so at time t = 8 hours the concentration of the medicine is increasing at a rate of 2.529 milligrams per liter per hour.

worked_solution.text: Differentiate the model to get the rate, \( C'(t) = \frac{55 e^{- \frac{t}{8}}}{8} \).
With a calculator, \( C'(8) = 2.529 \) to three decimal places.
worked_solution.rule_named: evaluate the derivative at the instant

worked_solution.text: The value is positive, so at time t = 8 hours the concentration of the medicine is increasing at a rate of 2.529 milligrams per liter per hour.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the rate gives the direction of change
